note: Adapted from Hill's (1942) new-species description, the original in English; the title line reads in the OCR as 'Mirotermes (Mirotermes) halgoorliensis sp. nov.'. Distribution: Kalgoorlie, Western Australia (type locality), and Cunnamulla, Queensland. Only the alate is known (holotype in C.S.I.R.); soldier and worker are unrecorded. Froggatt 1898 described the alate of this species as the winged form of Eutermes tumuli; Hill corrected this on the basis of Mirotermes adults in the type series. Measurements in mm.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: A large species, distinguished by the large compound eyes and ocelli (Fig. 318) and by the very short, dense hairs on head, thorax and abdomen. Overall appearance similar to M. jarmuranus but easily distinguished by the larger size, larger compound eyes and ocelli, wider fontanelle, different antennal segmentation and absence of long hairs. Compound eyes and ocelli very large and protruding; ocelli not much longer than wide (0.17 × 0.20). Mandibles as in Fig. 319. Antennae 15-segmented; segment 2 shortest; segments 3, 4 and 5 subequal in length; the remaining segments long. Pronotum very large, about as wide as the head, distinctly wider than long, distinctly concave anteriorly, anterolateral angles narrow, the sides narrowed to the wavy posterior margin. Posterior margin of mesonotum and metanotum wide and rather shallowly emarginate. Wings dark smoky, radius very short; cubitus with 8 branches, of which 1—2 may branch again; media running above the middle of the wing, unbranched, very close to the cubitus. Measurements (mm): body length without wings 5.50—6.00; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.32—1.39; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.73—0.80; head width 1.35; maximum diameter of compound eye 0.44; ocellus length 0.20—0.22; pronotum length 0.69—0.73; pronotum width 1.32—1.35; forewing length 8.90—9.60; forewing width 2.65—2.90. The body length with wings is given in the original OCR as '-±2.00', with the figures incomplete, and has not been forcibly transcribed.
